title: Overexpose
description: A summer sky through umbrella pines, seen lying on your back beneath them, developed live on colour negative film. It opens on the normal print, deep cobalt behind dark pines; drag up to overexpose it by as much as three stops. The light is multiplied before the film sees it, and each layer of the negative climbs its own long soft shoulder, so where a phone sensor would clip the clouds to flat white the cobalt thins to a pale white-blue, the cumulus compress towards cream and keep their edges, and the shadows open. The diffusion and halation grow with the light over the shoulder.
intent: Genre spec idea 5, after Rinko Kawauchi's overexposed 6x6 colour (Utatane, Illuminance): show why film looks dreamy and digital looks cheap with one gesture, exposure, on real linear radiance through per-layer H&D curves and a print curve. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinko_Kawauchi
sources: HDRI: Stone Pines, Poly Haven, photographed by Greg Zaal (backplates Rico Cilliers), CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/stone_pines (8k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/8k/stone_pines_8k.hdr). Lying on the grass under the umbrella pines of the Villa Borghese and looking almost straight up: stereographic projection, 118 deg field, pitched +83 deg towards the zenith at yaw +15 deg from the panorama centre, rolled +10 deg, 1536 px square, so the two near pines' trunks run in from the lower corners and converge on their crowns overhead, more crowns close the top of the square round a patch of deep zenith blue, and the large cumulus bank fills the gap between them. (An earlier bake used Poly Haven's Tree Lined Driveway; two re-aims showed it has no cloud above about 60 deg elevation and no trunks reaching the zenith, so no near-zenith camera could give the frame a subject. Its passes, desun.py to reaim.py in tools/depth/bakes/overexpose, are kept for the record.) The sun stands behind a crown 22.6 deg up, about 15 deg past the top edge: it is the hidden sun, and its light reaches the frame only as the glow of cloud seen through that crown's gaps and the aureole of the sky round it. Nothing of the photograph's own sky is kept: the open sky is laid as a polarised dome, a function of the angle from the zenith alone (polarise.py), as a strong polariser takes it, its light pulled down and its chroma raised: a dense cyan-cobalt overhead (printing about rgb(26,101,174) at +1.33 EV and rgb(22,91,155) at 0 EV, hue 208-209: below +2 EV the open sky takes a lift that eases out by +2, added as light in its own share over the dome's own field, sky.png, so the normal print opens on a luminous cobalt rather than a navy and a cloud's thin edge never prints darker than the sky beside it) opening to a paler cobalt towards the low sky at the edges (about rgb(80,140,190) at +1.33), the median open sky about rgb(36,113,187), and at +3 EV still a clear blue, never lavender; laid on the shipped bake in the sky share alone (polarise.py --relay), so the cumulus keep their light, eased as a broad dome so the deep blue holds level overhead, times the hidden sun's aureole as a softened power law of the angle from it (crown.py), times grain matched to the earlier bake's (amplitude, grain size and channel correlation). The pines and the cumulus are solved from the HDR's own radiance through the camera, 3x supersampled (swap.py running foliage.py's and cumulus.py's solves; the HDR is scaled by 0.32 so its open sky and needles sit at the levels those solves were set on). The pines: each pixel is unmixed in linear RGB between the light behind it and the local needle colour, so the matte is the photograph's own sub-pixel coverage and the needle sprays, bare twigs and crown fringes are as fine as the lens left them; the ink is the needles' own light solved out of the mix, taken down by one gain so the median needle prints near-black at 0 EV and part-way to #141a18's hue, keeping its relief (about 2.5 stops) so the lit bark, needles and hollows open up as the exposure climbs; where a gap near the hidden sun handed the sky's blue to the solve, the ink's blue-over-red is held to half a stop over the needles' median. Ink and matte ship as trees.webp, laid over the sky after the Pro-Mist and the halation. The cumulus: the depth matte is the HDR's own, per pixel (blue-minus-red saturation lost against the local open sky), crisped at turret edges and solid where a bank is thick; the cloud's light keeps the photograph's luminance above lobe scale, and below it the HDR's own shade eased gently, so the bank seen from underneath keeps its relief, with the depth matte's lobe structure laid over it: each pixel's distance in from the bank's edge takes the thick body down and lifts the thin rim of every turret, most on the side facing the hidden sun. The colour follows that light lobe by lobe, from skylight blue in the shaded body (about rgb(146,170,197) at +1.33) to a warm cream on the lit rims just under the paper white. Within a few pixels of open sky the cloud's light keeps its luminance but takes its chromaticity from the local bank body and the sky's own share, and the edge is feathered over a pixel or two (defringe.py), so the holes and wisps carry no cream outline. The small cloud scattered over the upper sky, away from the bank, had solved as a confetti of hard-edged white flecks: the specks are taken out to open sky (the dome and its own grain) and the few real wisps laid back with a depth feathered at two scales, given a toe and kept translucent, their thin edges taking the local cobalt (wisps.py). Two clipped cypress tops on the bottom edge are cloned out of the HDR before anything is solved. Each open pixel is (1 - depth) x the dome plus depth x that light, so no sky chroma gets inside a bank. The cloud share (and the hidden sun's glow on the sky share) ships as scene.webp's alpha, the printer's sky hold, so the piece holds everything but the cloud back as it overexposes and the clouds climb the print's shoulder above the sky; a cloud highlight takes cloudWarm more red than blue before the paper-white cap, so the tops roll off towards #fff6ea and never reach 255. Shipped as log2 radiance -8.5..+2.5 in 8 bits with TPDF dither (scene.webp), with the diffusion and halation blurs baked from the visible scene (optics.png). Bake: tools/depth/bakes/overexpose/swap.py.
